related_questions.question: Can I have COVID without a fever?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is possible to have COVID-19 without experiencing a fever. While fever is a common symptom, studies have shown that a significant portion of individuals with COVID-19 do not develop a fever. For example, a review of early pandemic studies found that only 78% of people with COVID-19 had a fever, meaning nearly 22% did not. Symptoms can also vary depending on vaccination status and new COVID-19 variants.

Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing can also be a symptom, but is more likely to indicate moderate to severe illness according to the CDC.
